title: Quantile-based session imbalance mitigation for metering pipeline
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Investigate and implement a quantile-based mitigation layer in the metering ingestion pipeline to correct for session-level token-count skew introduced by hybrid (batch + interactive) request patterns and aggressive continuous-batching heuristics.
background: We observed recurring billing variance for customers with highly skewed session shapes. Long-lived interactive sessions with intermittent short requests get merged into large batches by the serving runtime's continuous batching heuristics, producing over-attribution for some sessions and under-attribution for others when prefix caching and speculative KV reuse are applied. Current heuristics (time-window + max-batch-size) don't account for distributional skew: heavy-outlier sessions disproportionately affect batch composition and token credits. Existing metering reconciliations (checkpointing and finalization) fix many cases but leave a residual customer-facing billing delta (~0.3-1% in tail workloads) that is unacceptable for enterprise customers under Reserved Capacity contracts.
proposed_solution: Add lightweight per-session token distribution sketches at the ingestion boundary (fixed-size quantile summaries) to surface session skew without full per-token retention.
Use a quantile-guided batch policy in the metering aggregator that flags batches with high inter-session token variance and splits them before KV-prefetch/aggregation to preserve fair attribution.

Implement a deterministic post-aggregation adjustment step: compute per-session scaling factors using the stored sketch and batch-level totals to re-assign speculative prefix credits in a reproducible way during checkpoint finalize.
Ensure idempotent checkpoint metadata (monotonic checkpoint id + canonical session fingerprint) to allow safe retries and replay-based reconciliation across sequencer restarts.
Expose new telemetry (per-batch variance, percentage of batches split by quantile policy, pre/post adjustment delta) and add regression checks to the billing audit job.
Design end-to-end tests that synthesize skewed session workloads including: intermittent micro-requests, long-running high-token sessions, mid-stream model-switch events, and client reconnects.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Pros: reduces customer-visible billing drift in skewed workloads, prevents a small number of heavy sessions from inflating credits for other sessions in the same batch.

Cons: introduces additional small CPU and memory costs at ingestion (sketch maintenance) and alters batching behavior which could slightly increase p99 latency for some small requests when split decisions occur.
Risk: incorrect scaling heuristics could underbill or over-correct. Mitigation: conservative default quantile thresholds, staged rollout, and strict A/B monitoring against a control group.
Operational complexity: new telemetry and reconciliation steps must be integrated into existing billing audits and incident playbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Metering pipeline reports per-batch variance metrics and the quantile-split rate in production telemetry dashboards.
End-to-end synthetic tests show <= 0.05% median billing delta and <0.2% 99th-percentile billing delta compared to an ideal per-token ground truth across representative skewed workloads.
Production shadow run for 2 weeks with canary customers shows no customer-impacting regressions and p99 latency increase <= 5% for small interactive requests.
All changes are covered by unit tests, integration tests, and a deterministic replay test that validates idempotency across sequencer restarts.
Billing audit job (daily) shows reduced tail billing anomalies for reserved-capacity customers in the test cohort.
Rollout plan and rollback mechanism documented in Confluence and sign-off received from Billing and SRE teams.
